data.title: IGL Q2 profit plunges 93% as higher gas costs erode margins despite record sales
data.description:
Indraprastha Gas Ltd (IGL), the country's largest city gas distributor, reported a sharp 93.5 per cent decline in standalone net profit for the September quarter as a substantial increase in input gas costs eroded margins, offsetting higher sales volumes and revenue.

Net profit fell to ₹24.38 crore in the second quarter of 2026-27 from ₹372.51 crore a year earlier, despite an 8 per cent increase in sales volumes and a 26 per cent jump in gross turnover.

The company said its average daily gas sales crossed the 10 million standard cubic metres per day (mmscmd) mark for the first time, rising to 10.06 mmscmd in the July-September period from 9.31 mmscmd in the corresponding period last year.

Gross sales turnover increased to ₹5,999.13 crore from ₹4,431.63 crore, reflecting higher sales as well as the impact of increased gas prices.

CNG volumes grew 9 per cent year-on-year during the quarter, while piped natural gas (PNG) sales rose 8 per cent, indicating continued expansion in demand across the transport and household segments.

However, the steep fall in profitability despite higher volumes and turnover highlights the pressure that rising procurement costs can exert on city gas distributors, particularly when increase in input prices cannot be fully passed on to consumers.

IGL operates city gas distribution networks across 34 districts in 11 geographical areas spanning Delhi, Uttar Pradesh, Haryana and Rajasthan.

Its infrastructure includes more than 30,000 km of pipelines and over 1,000 CNG stations, catering to more than 2.5 million CNG vehicles. It has also connected over 3.5 million households to piped natural gas.

data.title: Piyush Goyal Urges FMCG Firms To Join ONDC Push To Digitise 1.4 Cr Kirana Stores
data.description:
At a CEO roundtable in New Delhi, the minister calls for industry-wide collaboration to strengthen digital procurement, improve supply-chain efficiency and expand access to credit for neighbourhood retailers

Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal has called on FMCG companies and industry stakeholders to work together to accelerate the digitalisation of India's 1.4 crore kirana stores, as the government steps up efforts to strengthen the country's general trade ecosystem through ONDC's DigiDukaan initiative.

Goyal chaired a high-level CEO roundtable, Bharat Commerce Chintan Shivir, organised by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) and the Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC) at Vanijya Bhawan, New Delhi. The meeting brought together more than 40 senior leaders from leading FMCG companies to discuss a common roadmap for digitising procurement and improving the competitiveness of neighbourhood retailers.

The discussions focused on securing greater institutional commitment from FMCG companies, distributors and other stakeholders to promote digital procurement, streamline supply chains and improve access to services for small retailers.

DigiDukaan Focuses On Digitising Procurement

Unlike conventional kirana digitisation initiatives that primarily help retailers sell products online, ONDC's DigiDukaan focuses on digitising them as buyers. The platform aims to enable neighbourhood stores to discover and order products from multiple brands, distributors and wholesalers through a single digital interface.

Retailers can access greater transparency on pricing, trade schemes and product availability while continuing to work with their existing distribution partners. The initiative also aims to create a common digital infrastructure that can eventually connect kiranas with shared logistics, micro-warehousing and formal credit facilities.

Senior representatives from Hindustan Unilever, Coca-Cola India, ITC, P&G, Marico, CavinKare, Pidilite, Britannia, Adani Wilmar, LT Foods, Anmol Industries, Haldiram's, Emami, Veeba and Nilon's attended the roundtable, along with logistics providers, technology partners and ONDC network participants.

Common Digital Identity, Logistics And Credit In Focus

The roundtable identified five key priorities for strengthening India's general trade ecosystem.

These include developing a common digital identity for kirana stores to facilitate seamless engagement with multiple brands and service providers; creating shared logistics and micro-warehousing infrastructure to improve distributor reach and enable reliable next-day replenishment; and expanding access to formal credit through financing solutions linked to digital procurement and transaction records.

The discussions also highlighted the need to simplify technology integration through plug-and-play Distributor Management System (DMS) connectors, standardised product catalogues and common digital interfaces.

Another key priority is realigning commercial incentives for FMCG sales teams, distributors and channel partners to encourage digital ordering, wider retail coverage and sustained adoption of the platform.

DigiDukaan Connects 21,000 Retailers With 450 Brands

DigiDukaan has connected more than 21,000 retailers with over 450 brands across Hyderabad, Jaipur and Mumbai as of September 2026, compared with over 12,000 retailers in the previous quarter.

Hyderabad accounts for more than 16,000 onboarded retailers, with monthly repeat ordering rates ranging between 73% and 78%. An initial ONDC study also found that 40% of surveyed retailers reported lower inventory holdings for products procured through DigiDukaan, indicating the potential for improved working capital efficiency.

Goyal said the initiative demonstrated how open digital infrastructure, designed around the needs of small retailers, could accelerate adoption.

"By making procurement simpler and more transparent while strengthening our distributors, we can help kiranas free up working capital and grow," he said, inviting the FMCG industry to work together to extend the initiative across the country. He also called for DigiDukaan to become a case study for the world to learn from India's digital commerce model.

DPIIT Secretary Amardeep Singh Bhatia said open digital infrastructure had an important role in accelerating the digitalisation of India's retail ecosystem, particularly its extensive network of kirana stores.

He said DigiDukaan demonstrated how an open and interoperable network could help neighbourhood retailers access digital procurement opportunities and participate more effectively in the evolving digital economy.

FMCG Brands And Technology Partners Expand Participation

ONDC Managing Director and CEO Vibhor Jain said that while distributors had increasingly adopted digital tools for billing, printing and order placement, many neighbourhood retailers continued to depend on manual processes.

DigiDukaan aims to address this gap by digitising kiranas as buyers while strengthening, rather than replacing, the existing distributor network, he said. Jain added that the objective was to create a shared digital foundation through which retailers could access multiple brands, transparent trade schemes, faster replenishment and, eventually, formal credit.

Among FMCG companies participating through their distribution networks are HUL, Marico, Colgate-Palmolive, Emami and Amul. ITC, Tata Consumer Products and Britannia are at various stages of integration or discussions.

On the technology front, Paytm for Business, Qwipo and Mulltiply.ai are live on the network, while Bizom, Botree, QuIDPe and ENS are progressing towards integration. Logistics and warehousing partners, including ElasticRun, Shiprocket, India Post and Moeving, are also part of the expanding ecosystem.

The National Traders' Welfare Board, chaired by Sunil J. Singhi, is working with ONDC to accelerate adoption among kirana retailers by mobilising local trade associations and strengthening retailer participation.

For its next phase, ONDC plans to deepen brand and distributor participation in Mumbai, particularly North Mumbai, while strengthening operations in its existing markets.

data.title: Sebi Fines CDSL Rs 1 Crore For Compliance Lapses
data.description:
The market regulator flags deficiencies in pledge request communication, cybersecurity controls, vulnerability patching and disaster recovery operations following an inspection for FY24

Markets regulator Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) has imposed a penalty of Rs 1 crore on Central Depository Services (India) (CDSL) for multiple regulatory compliance lapses, including deficiencies in pledge request communication, cybersecurity safeguards and disaster recovery operations.

In an adjudication order dated October 30, Sebi said its inspection of CDSL for FY2023-24 had revealed several instances of non-compliance with regulatory requirements. The depository has been directed to pay the penalty within 45 days, failing which recovery proceedings may be initiated.

Pledge Rejection Communication Under Scanner

One of the key violations related to CDSL's failure to communicate the reasons for rejecting pledge requests to the depository participants (DPs) of both the pledgor and the pledgee.

According to the findings reported in the adjudication proceedings, the regulator identified 92 instances of such failures during the inspection period. CDSL submitted that its earlier system did not make it mandatory to record rejection reasons. The company subsequently introduced system changes to address the deficiency.

Sebi also flagged non-compliance with prescribed procedures governing Client Unpaid Securities Accounts (CUSA). The shortcomings included deficiencies in freezing and unfreezing securities, inadequate system-level checks and failure to follow certain instructions issued by stock exchanges.

Cybersecurity And Disaster Recovery Lapses

The regulator also identified shortcomings in CDSL's information technology and cybersecurity framework.

These included inadequate measures to prevent unauthorised transmission of data and incomplete implementation of Data Loss Prevention safeguards. Sebi found that security information and event management logs were being collected at the primary data centre during a disaster recovery drill instead of the designated disaster recovery site.

Further, CDSL had failed to patch identified software vulnerabilities within the prescribed timeline. Its Vulnerability Assessment and Penetration Testing (VAPT) exercise was also found to be inadequate, as it did not cover all relevant domains and external applications.

Sebi Flags Implications For Market Integrity

Emphasising the systemic importance of depositories, Sebi observed that the deficiencies affected CDSL's core responsibilities relating to electronic record-keeping, dematerialisation and securities ownership transfers.

The regulator noted that such lapses could have implications not only for individual investors but also for the integrity and stability of the Indian securities market.

Sebi, however, took note of the remedial measures subsequently undertaken by CDSL while determining the penalty. It imposed the Rs 1 crore fine under Section 15HB of the Sebi Act, 1992.

In July this year, Sebi had also imposed a separate Rs 1 crore penalty on CDSL over cybersecurity shortcomings linked to a malware attack that disrupted its systems in November 2022.

data.title: Ramkrishna Forgings Q2 Revenue Jumps 55% To Rs 1,405 Cr, PAT At Rs 71 Cr
data.description:
The EBITDA margin improved to 18.2 per cent from 13.5 per cent in the year-ago quarter, an expansion of 473 basis points

Ramkrishna Forgings reported a 54.9 per cent year-on-year (Y-o-Y) increase in consolidated revenue from operations to Rs 1,405.42 crore in the second quarter of financial year 2026-27 (Q2FY27), supported by healthy domestic demand and resilient export market activity.

The company's profit after tax (PAT) stood at Rs 70.59 crore in Q2FY27, compared with a loss of Rs 9.50 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous financial year. PAT had stood at Rs 47 crore in the preceding quarter.

Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) more than doubled to Rs 256.23 crore in Q2FY27, compared with Rs 122.54 crore a year earlier, registering a growth of 109.1 per cent.

The EBITDA margin improved to 18.2 per cent from 13.5 per cent in the year-ago quarter, an expansion of 473 basis points.

For the first half of FY27, the company's consolidated revenue increased 36.4 per cent to Rs 2,622.09 crore, compared with Rs 1,922.79 crore in H1FY26.

EBITDA for the first half rose 75.1 per cent to Rs 474.70 crore, while the EBITDA margin improved to 18.1 per cent from 14.1 per cent in the corresponding period last year.

PAT for H1FY27 stood at Rs 117.47 crore, compared with Rs 2.29 crore in the year-ago period.

Commenting on the results, Naresh Jalan, Managing Director of Ramkrishna Forgings, said domestic demand remained healthy, supported by firm commercial vehicle production schedules, while customer activity across key export markets remained resilient.

The company is also expanding its manufacturing capabilities. Its forged wheels facility near Chennai, established through a joint venture with Titagarh Rail Systems, is nearing commercial production. The project is expected to expand its presence in the Indian Railways supply chain.

The company is also ramping up its casting operations and adding capacities and value-added products to serve customers across passenger vehicles, electric vehicles and industrial applications.

During the quarter, the promoters completed the conversion of warrants, infusing Rs 150 crore into the company to support its balance sheet and ongoing business requirements.

Looking ahead, Ramkrishna Forgings is seeking to expand its presence in non-ferrous forgings, including aluminium, titanium, Inconel and Nimonic grades. These materials are intended for high-technology applications across aerospace, robotics and semiconductors.

Jalan said the company's focus would remain on improving capacity utilisation, disciplined execution and strengthening its balance sheet as it pursues long-term growth opportunities.

data.title: Infosys Adds 10,000 Seats With 1.1 Mn Sq Ft Expansion In Hyderabad
data.description:
he 1.1 million sq ft expansion will add 10,000 seats at the 450-acre Pocharam campus, taking its total built-up area to 5.68 million sq ft and supporting over 13,000 additional employees under a hybrid work model.

Infosys has expanded its Pocharam Development Centre in Hyderabad with a new 1.1 million sq ft software development block, adding 10,000 seats as the IT services company looks to scale its operations and strengthen its technology delivery capabilities in Telangana.

The facility, inaugurated on Friday in the presence of Telangana Deputy Chief Minister Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka and IT and Industries Minister Duddilla Sridhar Babu, takes the company's built-up area at the 450-acre Pocharam campus to approximately 5.68 million sq ft.

The new block will enable Infosys to support an additional workforce of more than 13,000 employees under its hybrid working model, the company said in a statement.

The expansion comes as technology services companies look to strengthen their delivery capabilities in areas such as artificial intelligence (AI), cloud computing, cybersecurity and engineering, amid growing enterprise demand for digital transformation.

Infosys Chief Financial Officer Jayesh Sanghrajka said Hyderabad had played an important role in the company's growth and that the expanded facility would increase its capacity to scale operations and develop specialised talent.

"As enterprises accelerate their adoption of AI, the campus will serve as a strategic hub that brings together world-class talent, infrastructure and technology capabilities to deliver complex transformation programmes for global clients," Sanghrajka said.

The Pocharam Development Centre currently has seven software development blocks, with a combined built-up area of approximately 4.58 million sq ft. The latest addition will further expand its delivery footprint in Hyderabad.

The centre caters to global clients across banking, financial services and insurance (BFSI), retail, life sciences and manufacturing. Its expanded operations will focus on strengthening capabilities in AI, cloud, cybersecurity, engineering and next-generation digital services.

The facility also incorporates energy-efficient infrastructure, including radiant cooling systems, smart lighting, rainwater harvesting and wastewater reuse. It has been designed with natural daylight, flexible workspaces, collaborative areas and employee wellness facilities.

Vikramarka said the expansion reflected Hyderabad's growing position as a destination for global technology companies, supported by infrastructure development and a skilled workforce.

"Investments of this scale reinforce Hyderabad's position as a preferred destination for global enterprises and advance our vision of a future-ready, innovation-driven economy," he said.

data.title: Aditya Birla Capital Q2 Profit Jumps 38%, Housing Finance PBT Surges 73%
data.description:
NBFC disbursements rose 12 per cent as overall lending assets expanded to Rs 2.34 lakh crore by September-end

Aditya Birla Capital reported a 38 per cent year-on-year increase in consolidated profit attributable to owners to Rs 1,288 crore for the September quarter of FY27, compared with Rs 933.5 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. The growth was supported by expansion across its lending and financial services businesses.

Consolidated revenue from operations rose 32.2 per cent year on year to Rs 14,003 crore from Rs 10,594 crore a year earlier. On a sequential basis, profit increased 9.62 per cent from Rs 1,174.70 crore in the June quarter, while revenue grew 14.97 per cent from Rs 12,179.54 crore.

Total expenses increased 30.07 per cent year on year to Rs 12,324.10 crore during the quarter, compared with Rs 9,474.99 crore in the year-ago period. Sequentially, expenses rose 15.27 per cent from Rs 10,691.74 crore recorded in the June quarter.

The company’s overall lending assets under management, covering its NBFC and housing finance businesses, increased 32 per cent year on year and 7 per cent sequentially to Rs 2,33,930 crore as of September 30, 2026. Both businesses recorded higher AUM and disbursements during the quarter.

The NBFC business reported a 26 per cent year-on-year increase in AUM to Rs 1,76,557 crore, while disbursements rose 12 per cent to Rs 24,708 crore. Profit before tax increased 41 per cent year on year to Rs 1,352 crore during the September quarter.

Housing finance recorded faster growth, with AUM rising 50 per cent year on year and 11 per cent sequentially to Rs 57,373 crore. Disbursements increased 55 per cent year on year and 19 per cent sequentially to Rs 8,957 crore, while profit before tax rose 73 per cent to Rs 335 crore.

Asset Management Performance

In asset management, quarterly average mutual fund AUM increased 4 per cent year on year to Rs 4,41,787 crore during the quarter. Equity quarterly average AUM grew 9 per cent to Rs 2,09,230 crore, while profit after tax for the business stood at Rs 221 crore.

The company also reported growth across its insurance businesses during the first half of FY27. Individual first-year premium in life insurance increased 25 per cent year on year to Rs 2,342 crore, while gross written premium in health insurance rose 48 per cent to Rs 4,543 crore.

Aditya Birla Capital’s digital platforms also expanded during the quarter, with its direct-to-consumer platform ABCD recording around 1.3 crore customer acquisitions as of September 30, 2026. The company’s business-to-business platform Udyog Plus crossed 24 lakh registrations.

Udyog Plus, which caters to the micro, small and medium enterprises ecosystem, had an AUM of Rs 7,262 crore at the end of the quarter. Across its businesses, Aditya Birla Capital had a network of 1,822 branches as of September 30.

Shares of Aditya Birla Capital ended 2.19 per cent higher at Rs 366.20 on October 30, gaining Rs 7.85 during the session. The stock has risen 2.17 per cent year to date and 16.91 per cent over the past year.

data.title: Jio Platforms Reports 14% Q2 Profit Growth In First Results After IPO
data.description:
Revenue from operations rises 11.4 per cent to Rs 40,475 crore as 5G subscribers cross 300 million and fixed broadband base reaches 30 million

Jio Platforms has delivered double-digit growth in profit and revenue in its first quarterly results since its stock market listing, with consolidated profit after tax (PAT) rising 13.7 per cent year on year to Rs 8,387 crore in Q2 FY27. The company, which raised Rs 30,188 crore through its initial public offering (IPO), reported its results two days after its shares began trading on the stock exchanges on 28 October.

Revenue from operations increased 11.4 per cent to Rs 40,475 crore in the September quarter, against Rs 36,332 crore in the corresponding period last year. The figure was also 3.3 per cent higher than the Rs 39,173 crore recorded in Q1 FY27.

Profit after tax increased 8 per cent sequentially from Rs 7,764 crore in the June quarter. Gross revenue, which includes revenue beyond operations, stood at Rs 47,485 crore, up 11.3 per cent year on year from Rs 42,652 crore and 3.3 per cent quarter on quarter from Rs 45,961 crore.

The earnings growth came alongside an improvement in operating margins. Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (Ebitda) rose 16.6 per cent year on year to Rs 21,879 crore from Rs 18,757 crore. On a sequential basis, Ebitda increased 4.9 per cent from Rs 20,865 crore.

Ebitda margin expanded to 54.1 per cent from 51.6 per cent a year earlier, a gain of 250 basis points. The margin was 53.3 per cent in the preceding quarter. Jio Platforms attributed the improvement to revenue growth, operating leverage and a stronger margin profile.

Earnings And Cash Generation

Profit before tax (PBT) increased 13.3 per cent year on year to Rs 11,259 crore from Rs 9,937 crore. The figure was 8 per cent higher than the Rs 10,427 crore reported in Q1 FY27.

Earnings before interest and tax (Ebit) grew 18.1 per cent to Rs 14,268 crore from Rs 12,082 crore in Q2 FY26. Its margin rose 200 basis points year on year to 35.3 per cent.

For the six months ended September 2026, revenue from operations reached Rs 79,648 crore, against Rs 71,364 crore in the corresponding period last year, an increase of 11.6 per cent. PAT rose 11.5 per cent to Rs 16,151 crore from Rs 14,485 crore, while Ebitda increased 15.9 per cent to Rs 42,744 crore from Rs 36,892 crore.

Cash generation also improved. Ebitda less cash capital expenditure stood at Rs 32,130 crore in the first half of FY27, nearly double the Rs 16,216 crore reported in the year-ago period. The company defines cash capital expenditure as cash outflow on property, plant and equipment, spectrum and other intangible assets, net of disposal proceeds.

5G And Broadband Expansion

Jio Platforms' customer base reached 542.4 million at the end of September, compared with 506.4 million a year earlier. The company added 9.1 million customers during the quarter, against 8.3 million in Q2 FY26. Monthly churn declined to 1.6 per cent from 1.9 per cent in the year-ago quarter.

Average revenue per user (ARPU) increased 3.5 per cent year on year to Rs 218.8 from Rs 211.4. It also rose from Rs 215.6 in Q1 FY27. The company said promotional offers for fixed broadband customers partly offset the benefits of a better subscriber mix and higher usage.

The 5G subscriber base crossed 300 million in September, with 66 million additions over the preceding 12 months. The technology accounted for around 56 per cent of Jio's total wireless traffic.

The fixed broadband base reached 30 million subscribers, following the addition of 7.3 million connections over the past year. Jio AirFiber accounted for 15.1 million of these subscribers and contributed more than 75 per cent of fixed broadband additions during the period.

Data consumption continued to rise alongside subscriber growth. Total data traffic increased 22.1 per cent year on year to 71.3 billion GB in Q2 FY27. Monthly data consumption per customer reached 44.2 GB, compared with 38.7 GB in the corresponding quarter last year.

IPO Proceeds And Debt

Jio Platforms' market debut on 28 October marked its entry into the listed market. The IPO, which comprised a fresh issue of 27 crore equity shares at Rs 1,119 apiece, generated gross proceeds of Rs 30,188 crore after the employee discount.

The company has allocated a substantial portion of the net proceeds towards reducing borrowings at its material subsidiary, Reliance Jio Infocomm. Jio Platforms said Rs 27,500 crore had been used to repay, either fully or partly, the principal outstanding on certain external commercial borrowings. The remaining proceeds will go towards general corporate purposes, in accordance with the IPO prospectus.

The company is also positioning its digital services portfolio around emerging technologies. At India Mobile Congress 2026, it showcased Jio Call Agent, an artificial intelligence-based tool that can transcribe and summarise calls, and JioFrames, a smart camera product with voice assistance, live translation and other connected features.

Jio Platforms Managing Director Akash M Ambani said the latest results reflected the expansion of the company's 5G network and broadband and digital services. He also identified satellite communications, 6G intellectual property and artificial intelligence integration across voice and data services as areas for future investment.

data.title: Syrma SGS Q2 Net Profit Jumps 87%, Revenue Rises 73%
data.description:
Strong automotive, industrial and export demand drives record quarterly performance, with exports jumping 91 per cent despite industry-wide component supply constraints.

Syrma SGS Technology posted its highest-ever quarterly performance in the September quarter of FY27, with consolidated net profit rising 87.2 per cent year-on-year to Rs 124.2 crore, supported by strong growth across its automotive, industrial and export businesses.

Revenue from operations increased 73.2 per cent to Rs 1,999.5 crore in the second quarter, compared with the year-ago period, while earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) rose 63.9 per cent to Rs 203.1 crore from Rs 124 crore, according to the company's earnings release dated October 30.

The electronics systems design and manufacturing (ESDM) company attributed the growth to robust demand from the automotive and industrial segments, alongside a sharp rise in exports, despite industry-wide component supply constraints.

Jasbir Singh Gujral, Managing Director at Syrma SGS Technology, said the company had reached the milestone of Rs 2,000 crore in quarterly revenue while navigating component shortages across the industry.

Exports emerged as a major growth driver, with revenue from overseas markets climbing 91 per cent year-on-year to Rs 513.8 crore. Exports accounted for 26 per cent of operating revenue during the quarter.

Among business segments, automotive revenue grew 91 per cent to Rs 516.9 crore, contributing 26 per cent to operating revenue, compared with 24 per cent in the corresponding quarter last year.

The industrials business recorded an 86 per cent increase in revenue to Rs 493.5 crore, accounting for 25 per cent of operating revenue.

The consumer segment remained the company's largest business by revenue, growing 57 per cent to Rs 572.7 crore. However, its contribution to operating revenue declined to 29 per cent from 32 per cent a year earlier.

Revenue from the IT and railways segment rose 69 per cent to Rs 272.7 crore, while healthcare revenue increased 61 per cent to Rs 134 crore.

Despite the strong revenue and profit growth, the company reported a sequential moderation in operating margins. EBITDA margin stood at 10.2 per cent in the September quarter, compared with 11 per cent in the June quarter. The profit after tax (PAT) margin also declined to 6.2 per cent from 6.6 per cent sequentially.

On a year-on-year basis, EBITDA margin contracted 58 basis points, while PAT margin improved 47 basis points.

Commenting on the first-half performance, Gujral said revenue grew 71 per cent and profit after tax nearly doubled, reflecting the company's execution capabilities.

He added that Syrma SGS had fulfilled customer commitments while reducing its working capital cycle to 63 days and turning operating cash flow positive during the first half of FY27.

data.title: CCI Clears Prosus’ $100 Mn Investment In Sachin Bansal-Led Navi
data.description:
Sachin Bansal, cofounder and executive chairman of Navi, said the partnership was significant given his association with Naspers and the Prosus Group spanning more than a decade

The Competition Commission of India (CCI) has approved Prosus’ investment in Navi, allowing the global investment firm to acquire a minority stake in the fintech company founded by Sachin Bansal.

The approval follows Prosus’ USD 100 million investment in Navi, which marked the startup’s first institutional fundraise. The transaction was subject to regulatory approvals and customary closing conditions.

As per a media report, the CCI described Navi as the holding company of a group offering financial services through a single consumer-facing mobile application. Its subsidiaries provide digital financial products accessible through mobile devices.

Navi did not disclose the valuation at which Prosus invested, the stake being acquired or the planned use of the funds.

Sachin Bansal, cofounder and executive chairman of Navi, said the partnership was significant given his association with Naspers and the Prosus Group spanning more than a decade. He added that the investment reflected confidence in the financial services institution the company was building.

Prosus said it was backing Navi because of its large user base, multiple business lines and technology-led approach. Ashutosh Sharma, head of Prosus India investments and M&A, noted that the company had delivered strong execution over the previous 12 months despite a challenging macroeconomic environment.

During FY26, Navi UPI strengthened its position in digital payments, while its lending arm, Navi Finserv, expanded its loan portfolio, with assets under management (AUM) crossing Rs 13,000 crore. The group also reported consolidated profitability in the fourth quarter of FY26, although it did not disclose the figures.

Navi Finserv's standalone net profit increased 32 per cent year-on-year to Rs 292.2 crore in FY26, while operating revenue rose 8 per cent to Rs 2,461 crore. However, its consolidated net profit declined 46 per cent to Rs 93.3 crore, even as operating revenue grew 17 per cent to Rs 2,691.5 crore.

Navi's IPO Plans

The investment comes as Navi is reportedly preparing to revive its public listing plans. As per a media report, the fintech company is considering refiling its draft IPO papers with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) by December 2026.

The proposed offering is expected to include a fresh issue of around Rs 3,000 crore. Navi has reportedly appointed JM Financial, Kotak Mahindra Capital, Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan as advisers for the planned IPO.

This would be Navi's second attempt to go public. The company filed draft papers with SEBI in 2022 for a Rs 3,350 crore IPO but later shelved the plan amid unfavourable market conditions.

Founded in 2018 by Sachin Bansal and Ankit Agarwal, Navi offers financial products across lending, insurance, mutual funds and UPI payments. Bansal stepped down as CEO in February 2025 and took over as executive chairman.

Navi said its UPI platform remained India's fourth-largest third-party application provider by transaction volume during FY26. Meanwhile, Navi Finserv's AUM crossed Rs 13,000 crore.

data.title: PB Fintech Q2 Net Profit Rises 42.5% To Rs 192.4 Cr, Revenue Grows 35%
data.description:
Policybazaar had onboarded 17.3 crore registered customers and nearly 3 crore transacting users

PB Fintech reported a 42.5 per cent year-on-year increase in consolidated net profit to Rs 192.4 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 135 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. Sequentially, net profit rose 18 per cent from Rs 163 crore in Q1 FY27.

The company’s operating revenue grew 35 per cent to Rs 2,177.7 crore during the September 2026 quarter, compared with Rs 1,613.6 crore in Q2 FY26. On a quarter-on-quarter basis, revenue increased 15 per cent from Rs 1,888.3 crore.

Including other income of Rs 100 crore, PB Fintech’s total income stood at Rs 2,277.6 crore. Total expenses increased 32.6 per cent year-on-year to Rs 2,067.7 crore, compared with Rs 1,558.8 crore in the year-ago quarter.

Segment-wise, the company’s core online business, comprising Policybazaar and Paisabazaar, reported revenue of Rs 1,336 crore, up 39.5 per cent year-on-year. Its new initiatives business contributed Rs 842 crore, registering 28 per cent growth.

In its investor presentation, PB Fintech said adjusted EBITDA increased 39 per cent to Rs 216 crore in Q2 FY27. Adjusted EBITDA margin remained unchanged at 10 per cent year-on-year.

PB Fintech’s total insurance premium grew 38 per cent year-on-year to Rs 9,385 crore during the quarter. Core online new protection premiums increased 38 per cent, while new protection premiums, covering health and term insurance, grew 42 per cent.

The company’s core renewal and trail revenue on a 12-month rolling basis stood at Rs 1,097 crore, up 41.7 per cent from Rs 774 crore in Q2 FY26. On a quarterly annualised basis, core insurance renewal revenue reached Rs 1,153 crore, marking 52 per cent growth year-on-year.

Policybazaar had onboarded 17.3 crore registered customers and nearly 3 crore transacting users. The platform has facilitated the sale of 7.7 crore insurance policies since its inception, the company said.

Paisabazaar reported an 80 per cent decline in loan disbursals to Rs 4,739 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 8,570 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. The platform recorded an annualised run rate of 4 lakh card issuances during the September 2026 quarter.

Paisabazaar expanded its user base to 6.3 crore people who had checked their credit scores, while its transacting customer base reached 82 lakh. The platform also recorded an average of 33 lakh monthly enquiries during the quarter.

Meanwhile, PB Fintech’s partner enablement platform, PB Partners, expanded its network to more than 5.7 lakh partners across nearly 19,000 pincodes. Its corporate insurance business booked 22,000 unique policies for enterprises and small businesses during Q2 FY27.

Shares of PB Fintech closed 1.76 per cent lower at Rs 1,000 apiece on the BSE on Friday.

data.title: Delhivery Swings To Rs 40.6 Cr Profit In Q2 FY27, Revenue Rises 19.8%
data.description:
Delhivery reported a pre-tax profit of Rs 39 crore against a pre-tax loss of Rs 53.2 crore in the year-ago quarter

Delhivery reported a consolidated net profit of Rs 40.6 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with a net loss of Rs 50.5 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. The logistics company also recorded a 27.4 per cent sequential increase in net profit from Rs 31.9 crore in Q1 FY27.

Operating revenue grew 19.8 per cent year-on-year and 4.6 per cent quarter-on-quarter to Rs 3,066.4 crore during the September 2026 quarter. Including other income of Rs 66.6 crore, total income stood at Rs 3,133 crore, compared with Rs 2,651.5 crore in Q2 FY26.

Total expenses increased 14.2 per cent year-on-year to Rs 3,093 crore from Rs 2,708.1 crore. Freight, handling and servicing costs, the company's largest expense head, rose 19.1 per cent to Rs 2,195.1 crore from Rs 1,842.9 crore.

Delhivery reported a pre-tax profit of Rs 39 crore against a pre-tax loss of Rs 53.2 crore in the year-ago quarter. A net tax credit of Rs 1.6 crore took its consolidated net profit to Rs 40.6 crore.

However, the year-on-year and sequential profit comparisons reflect the impact of the Ecom Express acquisition. As per a media report, Delhivery said its net profit in Q2 FY26 and Q1 FY27 would have been Rs 59 crore and Rs 62 crore, respectively, excluding the acquisition's impact.

Delhivery handled 32.5 crore express parcel shipments in Q2 FY27, registering 32.1 per cent growth year-on-year. Part truckload (PTL) freight volumes increased 14.2 per cent to 5.45 lakh metric tonnes during the quarter.

The company attributed express parcel volume growth to market share gains and demand across its diversified customer base. It also said October volumes exceeded initial expectations, providing an encouraging start to the December quarter.

Express parcel revenue increased 21.7 per cent year-on-year to Rs 1,961 crore, while PTL revenue grew 23.1 per cent to Rs 672 crore.

The company also reported improved realisations, or revenue earned per shipment or unit of freight. Express and PTL realisations increased 4.1 per cent and 5.6 per cent quarter-on-quarter, respectively, primarily driven by fuel-linked price increases and revisions to cover minimum wage inflation.

PTL realisations also benefited from new customer additions, repricing of existing accounts and an improved customer and shipment mix.

Adjusted EBITDA increased 48 per cent year-on-year to Rs 123 crore, with the margin improving to 4 per cent from 3.3 per cent in Q2 FY26. Reported EBITDA more than tripled to Rs 205 crore from Rs 68 crore, while its margin expanded to 6.7 per cent from 2.7 per cent.

Delhivery incurred no Ecom Express integration costs during the quarter, compared with Rs 90 crore in Q2 FY26 and Rs 17 crore in Q1 FY27.

The company expects service EBITDA margins in both its express and PTL businesses to improve through the remainder of FY27, supported by pricing revisions and higher network utilisation. It expects express service EBITDA margins to reach 16-18 per cent by the end of FY27, while PTL margins are expected to exceed 15 per cent.

Alongside its core logistics operations, Delhivery is scaling newer businesses, including its intra-city logistics platform Delhivery Local, international operations and financial services.

Delhivery Local currently operates across eight cities, including Delhi NCR, Bengaluru, Mumbai, Hyderabad, Ahmedabad, Jaipur, Pune and Chennai. Its annualised revenue run rate doubled from around Rs 100 crore at the end of Q1 FY27 to approximately Rs 200 crore.

The company has raised its FY27 exit annualised revenue target for Delhivery Local to Rs 280 crore from its earlier guidance of Rs 250 crore. It also aims to scale the business to an annualised revenue run rate of Rs 800-1,000 crore over the next two years.

Meanwhile, its financial services business is developing distribution channels for financial products across its vendor ecosystem and building co-lending partnerships.

Delhivery's board approved an equity investment of up to Rs 36 crore in its wholly owned subsidiary, Delhivery Fintech Distribution, in one or more tranches to support its operational and business requirements.

The company also highlighted its investments in artificial intelligence and automation to improve productivity and reduce operating costs. It said AI-led automation had reduced customer support and proof-of-delivery validation costs by more than 50 per cent without compromising output quality.

Delhivery has also started producing customised autonomous mobile robots through Delhivery Labs. It plans to deploy 100 self-developed autonomous pallet transportation vehicles by Q4 FY27.

Shares of Delhivery closed 3.02 per cent lower at Rs 386 apiece on the BSE.

data.title: Tata Motors Takes Control Of Iveco With 89.42% Stake Acquisition
data.description:
Initial settlement of the €14.40-per-share tender offer brings the Italian commercial vehicle maker under Tata Motors' control, with a fresh offer window for minority shareholders from November 2 to 6

Tata Motors has completed the initial settlement of its tender offer for Italian commercial vehicle manufacturer Iveco Group, acquiring an 89.42 per cent stake and bringing the company under its control. The acquisition was executed through Tata Motors’ indirect wholly owned subsidiary, TML CV Holdings B.V., according to a regulatory filing on Friday.

The transaction involved the acquisition of 238.16 million Iveco shares at €14.40 per share. Following the settlement, Iveco has become an indirect subsidiary of Tata Motors.

The development follows objections from some minority shareholders over the valuation of Iveco. Activist investor Petrus Advisers had questioned the offer price, arguing that it undervalued the company. In response, Tata Motors increased its offer from €14.10 to €14.40 per share earlier this month.

Minority Shareholders

With approximately 10.58 per cent of Iveco’s common share capital, excluding treasury shares, still outside Tata Motors’ ownership, the company will reopen the tender offer for five trading days, from November 2 to November 6.

The settlement for shares tendered during this additional window is scheduled for November 13.

Tata Motors said further details of the post-offer process would be announced in due course. These could include a voluntary purchase procedure, a Dutch legal squeeze-out or a post-offer demerger and liquidation. The company has not announced any further revision to the offer price.

The completion of the initial settlement has also resulted in changes to Iveco’s board and corporate governance structure.

Tata Sons Chairman N Chandrasekaran has been appointed chairperson of Iveco as a non-executive director. Tata Motors Group Chief Financial Officer P B Balaji and Executive Director Girish Wagh have also joined the board as non-executive directors.

Olof Persson will continue as Iveco’s chief executive officer. The six-member board also includes independent directors Guenter Butschek and Charles Nichols.

Corporate Updates

Iveco said all outstanding special voting shares had been repurchased for no consideration, leaving no such shares outstanding following the takeover.

The company has also advanced the announcement of its third-quarter financial results to November 3 from the earlier scheduled date of November 5.

Iveco reported revenue of €13.43 billion in calendar year 2025. The company employs approximately 33,000 people and operates 16 industrial sites and 22 research and development centres.

Its business operations span trucks, buses, powertrains and vehicle financing.

The acquisition brings together Tata Motors’ commercial vehicle operations in India and emerging markets with Iveco’s established presence in Europe and other international markets. Tata Motors has said the two businesses have complementary product portfolios and limited geographical and industrial overlap.

data.title: Yes, Alphabet Stock Got Hammered. No, We're Not Selling. — Barrons.com
data.description:
The Google-parent trades at a rare discount. If it simply returns to its historical valuation relative to Apple, the stock has nearly 50% upside.

By Al Root

Weak tech earnings are sending investors for the hills, so it may not be the best time for optimism. It also isn't a time to overreact.

Shares of Google-parent Alphabet have been hammered. Yes, there are risks — as there are with any company spending big on the artificial intelligence buildout. But Barron's is sticking with its call.

The company is still an AI winner. And now shares look shockingly cheap, trading at half the multiple that AI-wary Apple fetches.

We first picked Alphabet in November 2024, when shares traded at about $168, arguing then that fears of a breakup and the death of Google search at the hands of OpenAI's ChatGPT were overblown. That advice worked out well for readers who listened. With Alphabet stock at about $320 in November 2025, we reiterated our position.

That call looked solid until AI fears reemerged over the summer. The iShares Semiconductor exchange-traded fund peaked in June after Broadcom's disappointing earnings report that included weaker-than-expected guidance for its semiconductor business. (Guidance was for 200% year-over-year growth.)

That was also about the time that Alphabet announced an $80 billion stock sale, and days before SpaceX raised $75 billion in its record-setting IPO. Questions swirled: Were tech players spending too aggressively on AI? Will they make money? How are they financing the buildout?

Fear reached a tipping point earlier this week when Alphabet reported weaker-than-expected third-quarter earnings. Operating profit of almost $41 billion only grew 30% from a year ago. The problem? Wall Street was looking for $43 billion.

Shares fell almost 13% to $282.32 after earnings, pushing shares down more than 30% from the high of $404.47 reached in May. A $2 billion profit miss drove a $560 billion one-day decline in market value.

Barron's isn't here to argue with the market. But it is important to remain clear-eyed when volatility picks up. The earnings miss had little to do with AI.

Alphabet's cloud business more than doubled in the quarter, up from closer to 80% growth in the second quarter. Other cloud businesses are also seeing strong growth. Amazon.com's AWS business grew by 39% in the same quarter, faster than in the second quarter. Microsoft's Azure cloud business grew by 48% in the quarter — again — faster than in the second quarter.

And those performances came after other positive AI developments this week. AI growth at SpaceX was better than expected, and Anthropic's IPO registration statement showed relatively impressive profitability.

Alphabet's problem was that ad spending on Google search grew by 12%, down from 17% last quarter; ad spending on YouTube grew by 9%, down from 13%.

That raises two risks.

For one, it suggests that the economy isn't as strong as it once was. Results from other tech firms bear that out. Amazon.com's retail business was relatively weak in the third quarter, and Intel plunged partly because of an unexpected downturn in personal computers. Soaring memory chip prices have made them more expensive.

The economy is a risk that all investors need to continuously monitor. But it isn't the main factor that will determine Alphabet's stock direction over the coming months.

That comes down to the second risk: cannibalization. In other words, is Google's AI business eating search?

And that is where there is no shortage of opinion on Wall Street. Melius analyst Ben Reitzes called Alphabet's earnings evidence of secular decline. Most analysts skew positive, however. "AI mode [search] monetization is just beginning," Citi analyst Ronald Josey said. KeyBanc Capital Markets analyst Justin Patterson called the quarter an "air pocket," adding search monetization headwinds are "transitory." Deutsche Bank analyst Benjamin Black said AI is driving the strongest search-query growth in five years. He expects Alphabet to earn money from the search growth — eventually — likening it to when Meta Platforms first rolled out Reels, which initially took user engagement away from Facebook and Instagram's core feed.

Analyst commentary is worth considering. Valuation is a better reason to buy.

Alphabet trades for 18 times estimated earnings over the next 12 months, a discount to the S&P 500's 19 times multiple. Alphabet is the second cheapest stock of the Magnificent Seven. Nvidia shares trade at about 15 times.

Furthermore, Alphabet and Apple often trade at the same multiple, with a 25% discount being relatively normal over the past few years. Alphabet stock is now trading for less than 50% of Apple's 36-times multiple, the biggest discount between those two stocks over the past five years. If that 25% discount returned, Alphabet stock would trade at $400, up almost 50% from recent levels.

And what about Alphabet's free cash flow, which has been negative for two straight quarters? Well, Alphabet isn't a startup looking for profitability. It is spending on AI to build a new trillion-dollar business. If it shut off spending, free cash flow would return — but would investors really prefer that? Probably not.

data.title: Amazon's AWS Just Gave Investors A Big Growth Signal — And Gene Munster Thinks It's Only The Beginning
data.description:
Key points:
  • Munster said that the bigger signal came from Amazon's unusually long-term outlook, with management guiding for at least 40% growth in AWS in both 2027 and 2028.
  • He also pointed to Amazon’s management expecting the cloud business to eventually reach $1 trillion in annual revenue.
  • Munster argued that the length and magnitude of Amazon's AWS outlook are more important than the headline growth number.

Deepwater Asset Management’s Gene Munster believes that Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN) just gave investors a much bigger glimpse into the future of AWS than it typically does.

In a note on Friday, Munster outlined that Amazon’s AI infrastructure opportunity may be only getting started, pointing to Amazon’s management breaking pattern as far as the guidance for its AWS business is concerned.

Amazon shares ended with a decline of over 1% in Friday’s regular trade, but edged up by 0.2% in the afterhours session.

Two Years of AWS Guidance Is the Real Signal, Says Munster

AWS grew 39% year over year in the September quarter, roughly in line with expectations, according to the investor. However, he believes that the bigger signal came from Amazon's unusually long-term outlook, with management guiding for at least 40% growth in AWS in both 2027 and 2028, while adding that the cloud business could eventually reach $1 trillion in annual revenue.

Munster argued that the length and magnitude of Amazon's AWS outlook are more important than the headline growth number. He noted that while Amazon usually provides only one quarter of AWS guidance, the company offering visibility into two full years signals a level of confidence in AI-related demand that the company has rarely communicated this far in advance.

AWS grew 39% in the September quarter, and Munster believes the momentum could continue for years, and potentially, even for the next decade.

He argued that the broader message is that Amazon wants investors to look beyond its traditional retail identity and recognize the scale of the AI opportunity developing inside AWS.

"Despite all of the hype, we are just starting," Munster wrote, arguing that the AI movement could prove to be a "once-in-a-lifetime opportunity."

A $1 Trillion AWS Business Could Change Amazon's Investment Thesis

Munster said that the second major signal was Amazon's expectation that AWS could become a $1 trillion annual business within five to 10 years.

The investor believes that reaching $1 trillion in five years would require AWS to grow at an average annual rate of roughly 42%. Even taking the longer 10-year path would imply an impressive growth trajectory, according to Munster.

He added that this could fundamentally change how investors view Amazon. AWS currently accounts for roughly 21% of Amazon's total revenue, but Munster estimates it could represent about half of the company's revenue within five years.

Amazon also plans to begin selling its custom Trainium AI chips toward the end of 2027. Munster does not expect chip sales to become a major portion of Amazon's revenue, but sees the move as another indication that the company is positioning itself increasingly as an AI infrastructure player.

However, this would require enormous investment from Amazon, according to Munster, who expects the company’s capital spending to rise faster than current Wall Street estimates as it builds the infrastructure needed to support that growth.

What Retail Traders Think Of AMZN Stock

Retail sentiment on Stocktwits around Amazon trended in the ‘extremely bullish’ territory at the time of writing.

AMZN stock is up 4% year-to-date and 8% over the past 12 months. The S&P 500 ETF Trust (SPY) is up 11% over the past 12 months, while the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) is up 12%.

data.title: OpenAI's $30 billion funding ambition shrinks to $20 billion: What's worrying investors?
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 31 -- ChatGPT-maker OpenAI has reportedly pared down its funding round by $10 billion to $20 billion for valuation of $1.25 trillion, according to a report by the Financial Times.

This is a reduction from the previous target of raising $30 billion for a valuation of $1.4 trillion, as per a Reuters report.

It added that the Sam Altman led AI startup has slashed the funding round target to complete the process before Anthrpic's IPO so as to make the most of a largely similar investor base.

Reuters noted that US tech stocks fell amid worries over AI spending by tech companies - the Nasdaq index slumped 2.9% on Friday, down 7.8% from its all-time closing high on 6 October.

According to a report by Traders Union, investors are becoming less enthusiatic about large, private deals for artificial intelligence companies. Further, there is competition from rival Anthropic's initial public offering (IPO) and also increased scrutiny over AI spending, it added.

Sources told the publication that OpenAI was set to pull less than the reduced $20 billion target at Friday's deadline for commitments as some investors slashed their allocations.

Notably, the worries are sector wide. S&P Global Ratings on Friday downgraded Meta's AA- credit rating to Negative, in an "early step" amid growing pressure from the tech giant's increased artificial intelligence (AI) related expenditures, Bloomberg reported.

S&P in a statement said the AI spending related strain on Meta's balance sheet and rising leverage (earnings relative to debt) were key factors that led to the decision, it added. The move comes as investors scrutinize Meta's and other industry players' ability to generate tangible returns from the massive investments they've been plowing into the AI buildout.

The largest partcipant is expected to be a UAE consortium, which includes the Arab state-backed MGX. The deal allows the startup option to lease new computing power in the Gulf region, it said.

As per the report, other investors include Andreessen Horowitz, Coatue, Founders Fund, Sequoia Capital and SoftBank.

There is also expected to be a retail round for HNIs to buy into OpenAI during this $20 billion fundraising round, it added.

Founders Fund, OpenAI, Sequoia and SoftBank refused to give comments, while Andreessen Horowitz, Coatue and MGX did not immediately respond, as per the report.

data.title: Deendayal Port Authority bags 'Smart Port of the Year' award at Smart Logistics Awards 2026
data.description:
Rajkot, Oct. 31 -- Deendayal Port Authority (DPA), Kandla, has bagged the prestigious 'Smart Port of the Year' award at the Smart Logistics Awards 2026, organised by Maritime Gateway in Rajkot, recognising its efforts towards developing a smarter, more efficient and future-ready port.

DPA Chairman Sushil Kumar Singh congratulated the entire port fraternity, including port users, stakeholders, officers, trade unions, employees and dedicated shramiks, for their collective efforts and commitment towards the port's development.

The recognition comes amid DPA's ongoing efforts to strengthen its cargo-handling infrastructure.

On October 21, the port authority issued a Letter of Award (LoA) to Essar Ports Limited for developing a multi-purpose cargo terminal at Tuna Tekra, Kandla, at an estimated project cost of Rs 2,276.06 crore.

The project will be implemented on a Build-Operate-Transfer (BOT) basis under the Public-Private Partnership (PPP) mode for a concession period of 30 years, marking a step towards strengthening India's maritime infrastructure.

According to DPA, Essar Ports Limited emerged as the highest bidder through a global competitive bidding process, offering a royalty of Rs 61 per tonne payable to DPA. The terminal will be developed on the eastern side of DPA's Mega Container Terminal at Tuna Tekra, which is being developed by DP World under the PPP mode.

The project is expected to augment DPA's multipurpose cargo-handling capacity and support the long-term growth of domestic and export-import (EXIM) trade, the port authority said.

On the occasion, DPA Chairman Sushil Kumar Singh formally handed over the Letter of Award to V Srinivasan, Operating Partner-Infrastructure Vertical, and Ashish Rajgarhia, Chief Executive Officer of Essar Ports, in the presence of senior officials from DPA and Essar Ports Limited.

The terminal is designed to handle 18.33 million tonnes of cargo annually. The estimated project cost is Rs 2,276.06 crore, comprising an investment of Rs 1,552.57 crore by the concessionaire and Rs 723.49 crore by DPA

The facility will comprise four berths, each measuring 300 metres, providing an aggregate berth length of 1,200 metres. It is designed to accommodate Cape-size vessels of up to 1,70,000 deadweight tonnes (DWT), with a draft capability of up to 18 metres. Commercial operations are expected to commence by 2031.

The multi-purpose cargo terminal is expected to strengthen DPA's cargo-handling capabilities, improve the efficiency of India's trade logistics and contribute to port-led economic growth in Gujarat and the wider hinterland.

data.title: Nazara Tech invests ₹734 crore into UK arm for acquisition of Bluetile & Bestplay
data.description:
Nazara Technologies shares will be in focus on Monday, after the company announced that it has infused $77 million, or approximately ₹734.35 crore, into its wholly owned UK subsidiary, Nazara Technologies UK.

In an exchange filing, the Mumbai-based company said that it has paid the second tranche of its acquisition of Spanish gaming companies Bluetile Games and Bestplay Systems.

The company infused $77 million, or about ₹734.35 crore, into its wholly owned UK subsidiary, Nazara Technologies UK, on October 29 through a subscription to equity shares. The infusion is subject to compliance with applicable laws.

The following day, Nazara UK paid the same amount in cash to the sellers as the second tranche. The total consideration payable is $303.02 million, or about ₹2,990 crore.

The balance will be paid in the manner set out in the Amended and Restated Share Purchase Agreement. The company said it will provide an update in due course.

Bluetile and Bestplay remain wholly owned subsidiaries of Nazara UK and step-down subsidiaries of Nazara Technologies.

The filing was made under Regulation 30 of the Listing Regulations and follows the company’s earlier disclosures on the deal dated March 18, June 16, August 3 and August 6, 2026.

The shares of the company closed in red on Friday, falling over 1.50% as the trade came to a close for the week. The shares fell below the mark of ₹400 per share.

However, the company's shares have seen a major rise of over 51% over the past 6 months. The stock price now stands at ₹398 per share.

By Doug Busch

UnitedHealth Group stock has staged an impressive recovery from last year's selloff, but its current valuations suggest there are more gains ahead as the insurer's profitability accelerates.

Shares have rallied over 60% from their March lows near $256, bringing year-to-date gains to 24% alongside a reliable 2.3% dividend yield. But don't let its rally dissuade you from buying the stock — technical analysis suggests it has more room to run.

Momentum was recently reinforced following third-quarter results, where management raised full-year 2026 guidance. Wall Street consensus remains overwhelmingly constructive. Sell-side price targets are clustered in the mid-to-high $400s, compared with the stock's recent $409. That implies attractive risk-adjusted upside for a premier managed-care operator whose earnings power is firmly re-accelerating.

As a healthcare provider, the stock operates within an overlooked subsector of the broader healthcare complex that is demonstrating outstanding leadership. Over the trailing six months, the State Street Health Care Select Sector SPDR Fund, also known by its ticker XLV, has ranked as the top-performing major S&P sector, advancing 30%. But industry concentration is particularly evident in the iShares U.S. Healthcare Providers ETF, which has gained 26% so far this year and trades just 1% beneath its 52-week high. The fund cleared a $58 bull flag trigger two weeks ago, resolving a consolidation pattern that originated from an aggressive 11-of-14-week winning streak between April and July that generated a near 50% advance.

As the the XLV's largest constituent with a portfolio weighting exceeding 20%, UnitedHealth serves as the engine of this subsector advance.

On its multi-decade monthly timeframe, UNH successfully defended its rising 200-month simple moving average in both August 2025 and March 2026. This dynamic long-term baseline holds profound historical significance. It was last tested during the depths of the global financial crisis in the first quarter of 2009, an inflection point that launched a historic multi-year bull cycle from $16.18 to a record peak of $630.73 in November 2024.

Let's take a closer look at the daily and weekly charts to see what the price action is telling us.

Looking at the daily chart, UnitedHealth's ratio chart against the XLV has lagged since mid-July. However, price action continues to reflect resiliency. Over the trailing month, UNH advanced 12% after successfully testing and rebounding off its rising 200-day simple moving average. This primary impulse initiated in earnest on July 7, with a 9% gap-up that completed a bullish island reversal, closing just above the very round $300 number before propelling shares on a rapid $150 advance over the ensuing three months.

From those highs, the stock digested gains via a constructive double-bottom consolidation, which originally formed following a pullback sequence marked by a bearish filled-in candle and a doji on July 16 and 17. data.title: S&P cuts Meta’s credit rating outlook to negative as AI spending mounts
data.description:
S&P Global Ratings hinted on Friday, October 30, that it could downgrade Meta Platforms' credit rating within two years, as the company’s heavy spending on artificial intelligence (AI) strained its finances.

The agency lowered its outlook on Meta’s AA- credit grade to negative, according to a statement. S&P said the company’s rising leverage, which measures debt against earnings, also drove the decision.

“Meta’s ability to monetise its AI investments is more limited than that of its peers,” S&P said.

The agency added that it was unclear when the spending would produce enough revenue to cover rising costs. The outlook “reflects uncertainty around how long capex will remain elevated and free operating cash flow will be negative,” it said.

A negative outlook does not mean a downgrade is under way, but it signals that S&P could cut the rating within the next couple of years, but is not actively considering one now, according to a Bloomberg report.

The move came as investors seemed to question whether Meta and other technology giants could earn real returns from their huge AI building programmes.

The Nasdaq 100 index fell 3.5% on Friday, briefly entering correction territory, after disappointing tech earnings.

Meta’s AA- rating is the fourth-highest investment-grade score, so even a one-notch downgrade would leave it firmly in high-grade territory. Still, S&P forecast that Meta’s capex, meaning spending on long-term assets such as data centres, would reach $140 billion this year and exceed $225 billion in 2027.

It said leverage could climb above 1.0 times as soon as next year, from about 0.1 times last year.

Meta, however, disagreed with the assessment. “We respectfully disagree with S&P’s assertion about Meta’s AI monetisation capabilities,” spokesperson Kamran Mumtaz said in a statement. “We see significant product and business opportunities ahead of us, supporting our very strong credit profile.”

Earlier this month, Meta disclosed more than $800 billion in future spending commitments, almost half of them tied to leases that had not yet begun, largely for data centres and energy infrastructure.

According to a Bloomberg report, Chief Financial Officer Susan Li told analysts: “We expect to continue investing aggressively to support both our core business and emerging AI initiatives.”

data.title: Who is Bahram Vakil, the founder of AZB, succeeding Noel Tata as Trent chairman
data.description:
The Tata Group is set for a leadership change at Trent Ltd, one of its key retail businesses. Bahram N Vakil is set to succeed Noel Tata as the company's chairman.

The appointments were approved during the board meeting on October 29. Vakil’s appointment marks a shift from a business leader associated with the expansion of the group's retail operations to a corporate lawyer with experience in financial restructuring, insolvency and project finance.

The transition comes amid differences between the Tata Sons board and Tata Trusts over the group's governance and control.

According to the company's stock exchange filing, Vakil will assume the chairmanship on November 12, a day after Noel Tata steps down from the position. Noel Tata will retire as chairman and director at the close of business on November 11, following nearly 29 years of association with Trent. He will continue his association with the company as chairman emeritus.

Who Is Bahram Vakil?

Bahram Vakil is the co-founder of AZB & Partners, one of India's leading law firms. He has built his career in corporate law, restructuring, insolvency, infrastructure and project finance. He holds an LLM degree from Columbia University and is a member of the New York State Bar.

Vakil became part of the board of Tata Investment Corporation in March 2025, taking on the roles of vice-chairman and independent director. He was also reportedly considered for a position on the Tata Sons board during discussions over vacancies.

Over the course of his legal career, Vakil has advised distressed funds, insolvency professionals and domestic and international banks on restructuring and bankruptcy matters. He has also worked on large stressed accounts referred by the Reserve Bank of India for insolvency proceedings.

In 2023, Vakil served on the Insolvency Law Academy's Thought Committee on Bank Insolvency and was also part of an expert committee formed to recommend changes to arbitration law. He also chaired ASSOCHAM's National Council on Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code and Valuation that year. Vakil has also been recognised by international legal publications for his work in restructuring and project finance.

Noel Tata Stepping Down

Noel Tata will step down as chairman and director of Trent on November 11, after nearly three decades with the company. The board approved the transition at its meeting on October 29, in accordance with the Tata Group's governance guidelines relating to board composition and director retirement.

Noel Tata has been associated with Trent since 1997 and played a key role in the company's growth and expansion in India's retail sector. In its exchange filing, the company said his leadership had helped Trent achieve important milestones, strengthen its market position and deliver sustained growth for stakeholders.

data.title: Markets Espresso: The whole thing is that ki Bhaiyya...Sabse bada Rupaiyaa
data.description:
Tumko maloom hai ki yeh ek paisa kya hota hai? Ek-Ek paisa jama karo to ek rupya banta hai. Ek-Ek rupya jama karo to 100 banta hai, 100 jama karo to hazaar banta hai. Hazaar hazaar jama karo to lakh aur lakh se crore banta hai. Yeh ek paisa, ek crore ka beej hai. Jo aadmi beej ki parvah nahi karega, wo na to fasal uga sakta hai, na phal pa sakta hai!

Hello Espresso Lovers! We are back after what felt like a never-ending week with over 200 results and a barrage of developments besides them. You may wonder why I would begin with the late Kadar Khan's memorable lines from Dariya Dil (1987) before greeting you all? The lines may be a message to companies in a land far, far away that have embarked on incessant, eye-watering spending plans without any assurance that any of it will even return to them. And finally, it seems the investor community has started to take note and feel worried.

Perhaps this one meme is central to the entire episode of today. This is the question investors are finally beginning to ask the Magnificent Seven companies as they keep reporting their results. Just last year, the situation was the complete opposite. The more these companies spent, the bigger the capex guidance they announced, the faster the stocks ran. Investors thought the money spent would return faster than an answer generated by AI when given a prompt. Alas, that was not the case.

For a better part of this year, the spending plans were largely viewed positively as companies assured investors that this was being done only through their own internal cash flows. But then came debt. And then some more. Investors thought, okay, they are still generating enough cash to repay the debt. They'll be fine. But when this spending binge began to show up in their results, the warning signs began to flash, the proverbial Khatre ki ghanti began to ring, and investors began to ask questions they should have asked a lot earlier - Will this money ever return?

Take a look at Alphabet - Google's parent. For the first time in four years, its results missed expectations. In an ideal case scenario, investors would cut them some slack and say, it's alright, the law of averages would have caught up someday. But no. There was a bigger devil in the detail. Its free cash flow was negative for the second quarter in a row. Not just that, it was almost 4.5x higher than what analysts had anticipated. The result? Stock falls 13%, the most in a single day since its IPO way back in 2004. $500 billion of market value wiped out in a single day. Worse still, they plan on spending more next year - $300 billion!

And Alphabet is not a stray incident. Most of the big tech companies that have reported results so far have reported negative free cash flows this quarter. Meta reported one for the first time after listing this quarter, and the stock was duly punished by investors for it as well. The same is the case with Amazon - negative free cash flow of $7 billion in the same quarter last year. This time? Wait for it...negative $42 billion. The only one that stood out? Microsoft. Still reported positive FCF even though it dropped 27% from last year. The question is, for how long it remains in positive territory if spending continues the way it has been.

And then comes Intel. The perfect synonym for "dead-man walking" for a better part of this year. Once a legend, almost driven to the border of irrelevance, administration picks up stake, things start looking up, stock runs, and runs hard. Gains almost 250% in just 7-8 months. Then comes the moment of truth. Numbers. Weaker than estimates. In fact, way weaker. Guidance disappoints. The Israel factory incident drags a $600 million hit over the next two quarters.

When a stock that has not done much disappoints, the investors choose to look away. But when you run faster than your legs can take, the fall is steeper, deeper, and more brutal. A 29% drop on Friday, the worst day since the 1970s. That's one-third of your value gone in a matter of hours. The biggest loser? No. Not retail for a change. DONALD TRUMP! His administration's stake took a $12 billion hit as a result of this fall. Wonder what he has to say on Truth Social about this, since he has gloated enough and more about Intel's stock returns.

We brought this to you last week. The highlight of every earnings season. But this time around, there's something different. Usually, when a stock would deliver good/bad numbers, the reaction to it would be limited to a day, max two. This time around, stocks with good numbers have continued to move higher, while those with bad ones have just not stopped correcting.

Ather Energy is the best example of this. The stock had corrected 20% to 25% from its previous highs, due to routine profit booking. Then came the results. First-ever profit. Not just EBITDA, but PAT level as well. Add to that some capacity expansion plans and strong management commentary. The street was as joyous as it could be. A 27% move last week on the upside, the best performer on the Nifty 500, and back at new highs as well!

On the flip side, there is CarTrade Tech - the potential "wild child" of the market. A ₹1,600 IPO falls to ₹350, then goes back to ₹3,000 plus, and then falls from there again. For a company growing between 20% and 30% every quarter, a 10% growth quarter was difficult to digest for the market. Yes, the festive season shifted compared to the base quarter, but 10% was just not acceptable to the street. The result? Down 23% this week, the worst Nifty 500 performer, now down 35% from those very highs that it had surged to and made the market sit up and take note.

Financial educator, speaker and author, Alan Miltz gave a very popular quote: "Revenue is vanity, profit is sanity, and cash is king!" Right now, the big techs are showing complete disregard for the same King that once gave them the trillion-dollar crowns they now sit on. Majrooh Saab (the great late Majrooh Sultanpuri) was not a visionary for no reason that he wrote Sabse Bada Rupaiyaa all the way back in 1976, and those lines hold true more than ever 50 years later! The whole thing is that ki Bhaiyya… sabse bada rupaiyaa!

Festivities begin for Diwali next week - the festival of lights and from all of us at CNBC-TV18, we wish you all a happy, prosperous and joyous Diwali and New Year. We are only grateful for your love, appreciation and feedback, and we hope that the festival brings plenty of light to your lives and the new year turns out to be a lot better than what this one has been! We'll see you next week with the latest brew! Happy Diwali to one and all!

data.title: India aims to be globally competitive semiconductor powerhouse by 2047: MoD
data.description:
India aspires to emerge as a globally competitive, dependable and technologically self-reliant semiconductor powerhouse by 2047, with leadership in selected next-generation chip technologies, the defence ministry said on Friday.

The vision encompasses the development of a vibrant and sustainable semiconductor ecosystem, generation of high-value employment opportunities and delivery of inclusive societal benefits, it said.

The Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) participated in the Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave (ESTIC) 2026 at the Bharat Mandapam from October 27-29.

Inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the conclave with the theme ‘Creative Minds, Catalysing Science, Empowering Society’ was jointly organised by 12 ministries and departments under the guidance of the principal scientific adviser to the government of India, the ministry said in a statement.

The event showcased cutting-edge research, deep-tech breakthroughs, and thought-provoking discussions with Nobel laureates, global experts, policymakers and emerging leaders, igniting a new era of scientific leadership, it said.

The DRDO, as one of the key organisers, led the thematic session on ‘Semiconductors & Next-Generation Chips’.

Chaired by B K Das, Director General, Electronics and Communication Systems (ECS), the session brought together eminent leaders from the industry, academia, indigenous chip-development ecosystem and defence electronics.

“The discussions explored emerging developments in semiconductor technologies, purpose-built artificial intelligence (AI) system-on-chips (SoCs), intelligence at the silicon edge and the evolving microprocessor landscape, the statement said.

The session also highlighted DRDO's evolving role in enabling industries and startups to develop game-changing solutions, accelerate next-generation chip design and strengthen indigenous core technologies.

“India aspires to emerge as a globally competitive, dependable and technologically self-reliant semiconductor powerhouse by 2047, with leadership in selected next-generation chip technologies,” the ministry said.

The DRDO outreach stall at ESTIC 2026 showcased key initiatives, achievements, research programmes and contributions of the ministry towards science, technology and innovation.

It featured a diverse range of indigenous technologies developed by DRDO laboratories, including advanced communication systems, quantum technology prototypes, extreme-cold-weather clothing, PRABALA female full-body protector, passive and powered exoskeletons, portable hybrid energy management systems, high-power pulse laser diodes and scramjet engine technology, the statement said.

Semiconductor technology is a critical enabler of national sovereignty, economic strength and digital security. It plays a key role in advancing the vision of Viksit Bharat by 2047 and Aatmanirbhar Bharat by strengthening indigenous technological capabilities, the ministry said.

From communication devices and advanced sensing systems to sophisticated defence platforms, semiconductor chips determine the performance, efficiency and reliability of modern technologies.

Beyond chip manufacturing, technological self-reliance requires comprehensive capabilities in chip design, fabrication, testing, industrial-scale production and resilient supply chains, it said.
